At 6'6" tall, he plays at the [[power forward]] position. He also represents the [[Nigeria men's national basketball team|Nigerian national team]] in international competition. == Early life == Moneke was born in [[Abuja]], Nigeria, before moving to Canberra, Australia to begin schooling. His parents, Sydney and Eucharia Moneke, were diplomats of the Nigerian embassy. He attended Farrer Primary School and [[Lake Ginninderra College]] before traveling again throughout the world.{{cite web|title=Chima Moneke: la locomotora de Abuya|url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/319120-chima-moneke-la-locomotora-de-abuya.html|website=acb.com|access-date=24 June 2025|date=10 February 2022|lang=es}}{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Dutton|title=Chima Moneke ready to make NBA world take notice at Sacramento Kings |url=https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/7934435/the-world-doesnt-know-me-canberras-newest-nba-star/|website=canberratimes.com.au|access-date=24 June 2025|date=8 October 2022|lang=en}} == College career == In 2013, Moneke enrolled at [[Northeast Community College]] in [[Norfolk, Nebraska]], where he stayed for two seasons (2013–15). In his sophomore season he averaged 17 ppg and 12.1 rpg which led the team to a 25–7 record.{{cite web|title=FORMER NORTHEAST MEN'S BASKETBALL STANDOUT CHIMA MONEKE BECOMES A KING|url=https://northeasthawks.com/general/2021-22/releases/20220727otwuit|website=northeasthawks.com|access-date=24 June 2025|date=27 July 2022|lang=en}} He then transferred to the [[University of California at Davis]]. After his [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] season, he led the [[UC Davis Aggies men's basketball|Aggies]] to an [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] berth for the first time in school history in the 2016–17 season. He was named [[Big West Conference]] tournament MVP. In the tournament they defeated [[North Carolina Central Eagles men's basketball|North Carolina Central]] in the play-in game in which Moneke had 18 points and 12 rebounds. They would go on to lose to the #1 overall seed [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], where Moneke finished with 20 points and 9 rebounds. He averaged 14.6 points, 9.5 rebounds and 1.4 blocks per game with 14 double-doubles.{{cite web|first=Savannah|last=Haynes|title=Get to Know Chima Moneke|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/get-to-know-chima-moneke|website=nba.com|access-date=24 June 2025|date=6 October 2022|lang=en}} In the 2017–18 season, he averaged 18.4 points, 9.6 rebounds and 1.1 blocks per performance in 21 games with the Aggies. == Professional career == === Rouen Métropole (2018) === After not being selected in the [[2018 NBA draft]], Moneke signed his first professional contract with [[Rouen Métropole Basket|Rouen Métropole]] of the French [[LNB Pro B]]. After the season, he signed with the [[South East Melbourne Phoenix]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|NBL]] before it was blown off due to problems with his passport.{{Cite web |date=2022-07-18 |title=De la Pro B à la NBA, Chima Moneke retrace son incroyable ascension : "Le voyage a été compliqué mais la destination finale est encore plus savoureuse" |url=https://www.bebasket.fr/de-la-pro-b-a-la-nba-chima-moneke-retrace-son-incroyable-ascension/ |access-date=2022-07-19 |website=BeBasket |language=fr-FR}} === Denain Voltaire (2018–2019) === In November 2018, he would leave Rouen Métropole to sign for [[Denain Voltaire Basket|Denain Voltaire]], also from the French [[LNB Pro B]]. He averaged 14.3 [[point (basketball)|points]], 6.6 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and 1.7 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] in 27 games. === Béliers de Kemper (2019–2020) === In the 2019–20 season, he signed for the [[Béliers de Kemper]] of the French LNB Pro B, in which he averaged 15.8 points, 6.75 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game. The season was cancelled early due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]. === Orléans Loiret (2020–2021) === In the 2020–21 season, he signed for the [[Orléans Loiret Basket|Orléans Loiret]] of the [[LNB Pro A]], with averages of 12.5 points, 6 rebounds, 1.8 assists and almost a block per performance in the 21 games played.{{cite news |url=https://www.larep.fr/orleans-45000/sports/chima-moneke-l-ailier-de-l-olb-est-entre-dans-l-histoire-du-basket-cette-nuit_13982638/ |title= Chima Moneke, l'ailier de l'OLB, est entré dans l'histoire du basket cette nuit |accessdate=13 July 2021|date= 11 July 2021 |website=larep.fr |language=fr}} === Manresa (2021–2022) === On 13 July 2021, Moneke signed a one-year deal with the [[Bàsquet Manresa]] of the Spanish [[Liga Endesa]] and the [[Basketball Champions League]] (BCL).{{cite news |last=Skerletic |first=Dario |date=12 July 2021 |title=Chima Moneke reportedly in advanced talks to join BAXI Manresa |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/chima-moneke-reportedly-in-advanced-talks-to-join-baxi-manresa/ |accessdate=13 July 2021 |website=sportando.basketball}} He helped Manresa to a surprising season in the BCL as they reached the [[2022 Basketball Champions League Final Four|final]] where they lost to [[CB Canarias|Tenerife]] in the final. Moneke was named the [[Basketball Champions League MVP|MVP]] of the 2021–22 season after averaging 13.1 points per game.{{Cite web |date=2022-05-07 |title=Moneke named MVP of the Season |url=https://www.championsleague.basketball/21-22/news/moneke-named-mvp-of-the-season |access-date=2022-07-19 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} In the Spanish ACB, Moneke was named to the ALL-ACB 1st team after leading Manresa to the playoffs. He averaged 14.8 points per game on 53% shooting. He was second in the entire league in rebounding with 8.4 per game. He led the entire league in total steals (56), steals per game (1.6) and defensive rebounds.[[File:Semifinals 42a Lliga Catalana AON 2021 AON (Foto M.A. Chazo) (51429184386).jpg|thumb|right|Moneke with [[Bàsquet Manresa|Manresa]] in 2021]] === Sacramento Kings (2022–2023) === On 18 July 2022, Moneke signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]], uniting with Nigeria's national team coach [[Mike Brown (basketball, born 1970)|Mike Brown]].{{Cite web |last=Maher |first=Rory |date=18 July 2022 |title=Kings Sign Chima Moneke, Won't Bring Over Sasha Vezenkov |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/07/kings-to-sign-chima-moneke-wont-bring-over-sasha-vezenkov.html |access-date=2022-07-19 |website=Hoops Rumors |language=en-US}} On 6 January 2023, Moneke was waived by the Kings.{{Cite web |date=6 January 2023 |title=Kings Waive Chima Moneke |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-waive-chima-moneke |access-date=2023-01-07 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} === AS Monaco (2023) === On January 16, 2023, Moneke signed with [[AS Monaco Basket|AS Monaco]] of the [[LNB Élite]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web |last=Maggi |first=Alessandro |date=16 January [[double-double]] with 19 points and 13 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] in an 88-81 win against [[ASVEL Basket|LDLC ASVEL]].{{Cite web |title=LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne vs Baskonia Vitoria-Gasteiz |website=Euroleague Basketball |language=en-GB}} === Crvena zvezda (2025–present) === On June 24, 2025, Moneke signed with [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia]] (KLS), [[ABA League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web |date=June 24, 2025 |title=Crvena zvezda Sign Chima Moneke |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DLSaGi7oCfX/?igsh=MTU0MTVjYmJqeWdraQ==}} == National team career == He debuted with the [[Nigeria men's national basketball team]] in 2020, playing three qualifying matches for the [[Afrobasket]]. In 2021, he was summoned for the pre-selection to compete in the [[2020 Summer Olympics]].{{citation needed|date=January 2024}} ==Career statistics== {{Euroleague player statistics legend}} ===NBA===
